title: O002-P1 Temporal-Alignment Permutation Test Under Strong Affective-Inertia Baseline
purpose: Reconcile two observations: EPiC/Coles et al. 2025 found that real peripheral physiology usually improves predictions relative to simulated random physiology, while O002 found no incremental predictive value beyond stimulus/time plus immediately prior self-report. Test whether correctly time-aligned physiology is more informative than autocorrelation-preserving time-misaligned physiology even when it does not beat the strong baseline.
input: Exact frozen O002 feature table generated by analysis/case_external_replication_o002.py; no window or feature changes.
evaluation: Leave-one-subject-out, same participant folds as O002.

model.preprocessing: Same categorical one-hot, training-fold median imputation, and training-fold standardization as O002.
model.alpha_rule: For each held-out subject and target axis, reuse the alpha selected for the peripheral model in the frozen O002 primary result. Do not retune after permutation.

null_control.type: within-subject × within-video circular temporal shift of the complete 29-feature physiology vector
null_control.rationale: Preserves each induction's multivariate physiology sequence, marginal distributions and circular autocorrelation structure while breaking its alignment to current/prior/future affect and to exact time-within-video.
null_control.shift_rule: For each subject×video sequence with n>=4 rows, draw one circular shift uniformly from 2..n-2 when possible; for n<4 use any non-zero shift. The same shift is applied to all 29 physiology features as a vector. Training and held-out sequences are shifted independently using deterministic RNG.

primary_quantity: For each held-out subject and axis: mean over permutations of [MAE(time-shifted physiology) - MAE(real aligned physiology)]. Positive values mean aligned real physiology carries more predictive information than the autocorrelation-preserving misalignment control.
uncertainty: 5000 paired subject bootstrap resamples over the 30 subject-level primary quantities.
secondary_quantities: Frozen O002 baseline-vs-real-physiology delta is reported unchanged for context; it is not redefined.
Fraction of permutations where real aligned physiology beats shifted physiology.

decision.REAL_SIGNAL_BUT_NO_INCREMENT: Primary CI strictly above zero for at least one axis while the frozen O002 real-physiology model did not beat the strong baseline on that axis. Interpretation: physiology contains time-aligned predictive signal, but it is redundant/too weak to add utility beyond affective inertia and context.
decision.NO_ALIGNMENT_EVIDENCE: Primary CI includes zero for both axes. Interpretation: under these features/resolution/model, no reliable time-alignment information is detected beyond preserved physiology structure.
decision.SHIFTED_BETTER_ANOMALY: Primary CI strictly below zero for either axis. Treat as anomaly/model-mismatch requiring investigation; do not claim physiology is anti-informative.

firewall: This is a post-primary mechanistic sensitivity, not a replacement for O002 primary.
No causal claim about body-to-feeling mechanisms.
A positive real-vs-shifted contrast does not imply incremental predictive utility beyond the strong baseline.
novelty_context: Designed in response to Coles et al. 2025 (Royal Society Open Science, DOI 10.1098/rsos.241778), which used random and mean-rating baselines, found degradation under simulated-random physiology, and explicitly identified stronger baselines preserving continuity/temporal variability/autocorrelation as an open benchmarking direction.
